title: Why does an ionic crystal fracture when struck?
question: Which explanation best accounts for the brittleness of ionic solids?

options.text: Their ions become neutral when the lattice shifts, so the crystal loses all attraction.
The ions are free to slide over one another because the lattice contains no strong forces.
Displacement can bring like-charged ions close together; their repulsion can cause the lattice to fracture.
The crystal fractures because its ions share electrons and form weak covalent bonds.

explanation:
Ionic crystals are held together by strong electrostatic attractions. When layers shift, like charges can become adjacent and repel strongly, causing fracture. Option B incorrectly describes the ions as freely sliding.
